=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21138-21142 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The poller invokes the sandbox-only RB_JUDGE through the host-side Claude helper, so Claude rejects the call and the poller falls back to Codex.
  WHY: `claude_run` rejects host execution of RB_JUDGE with exit 75 (`host_run_forbidden`), preventing the poller's review-blocked judge from running on Claude.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:714-721 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The Claude preflight treats RB_JUDGE defaulting to Claude as requiring Claude CLI installation and credential setup on every poll run, even when the other poller judges use Codex.
  WHY: RB_JUDGE cannot execute on Claude from the host and immediately falls back to Codex, so these setup steps waste runner time and pool credentials.
- README.md:1884-1887, 1894-1896 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The README says the poller's RB_JUDGE runs on Claude, contradicting the sandbox-only host restriction and Codex fallback.
  WHY: Operators relying on the documented Claude behavior will see the poller fall back to Codex with `host_run_forbidden`.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:88-92 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: When `log_file` is `/dev/null`, the stderr tee duplicates the stream back to stderr instead of discarding it.
  WHY: The caller's expected stderr suppression does not occur because `tee -a /dev/null` writes its input to standard output, which is redirected to stderr.
- scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh:230-241, 276 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: Killing the progress-monitor subshell does not terminate its foreground `sleep` child, so waiting for the subshell can delay completion by up to the configured progress interval.
  WHY: The default `REVIEW_SANDBOX_PROGRESS_SECS` is 60 seconds, which can add up to a 60-second delay to each Claude review invocation.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- Requirement: "The new `poller_claude_judge` helper wraps the security-pass, integration, stall, review-blocked and wave judge calls." (PR Description) and "the poller's ... `RB_JUDGE` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` `poller_claude_judge`)" (README:1885-1887) — the poller's review-blocked judge should run on Claude.
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21139 (poller_claude_judge RB_JUDGE call) and scripts/ai_engine.sh:65 (_AI_ENGINE_SANDBOX_ONLY_ROLES).
  Evidence of absence: RB_JUDGE is listed in `_AI_ENGINE_SANDBOX_ONLY_ROLES` at scripts/ai_engine.sh:65, so `claude_run RB_JUDGE` unconditionally exits 75 with `host_run_forbidden` (scripts/ai_engine.sh:189-194). The poller's `poller_claude_judge` at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21139 calls host `claude_run RB_JUDGE` with no sandbox isolation, so it always falls back to codex at line 21141. The poller's review-blocked judge can never execute on Claude despite the PR description and README claiming it does. The review_autofix path (scripts/review_rb_judge.sh `review_rb_claude_run`) correctly uses the sandbox, but the poller path does not. Additionally, the orchestrate_poll.yml preflight (lines 714-721) installs the Claude CLI and fetches credentials whenever RB_JUDGE resolves to claude, wasting setup work that can never be used.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
